title: [Audit] System and hidden index access
description: The newest 1,000 requests against .kibana*, .security*, .alerts-* and other dot-prefixed indices, one row per index named — privileged data access that deserves a second look. Backing indices of ordinary data streams (.ds-logs-…) and shard-level copies of a request are left out. An Identity that reads as an opaque id is a principal whose events carry no email and no key name — usually an organisation-level Elastic Cloud API key, which the audit stream records only by its id.
esql: FROM logs-elastic_cloud.serverless_audit.otel-default | WHERE attributes.elasticsearch.audit.indices IS NOT NULL | MV_EXPAND attributes.elasticsearch.audit.indices | WHERE ((attributes.elasticsearch.audit.indices LIKE ".*" AND NOT attributes.elasticsearch.audit.indices LIKE ".ds-*") OR attributes.elasticsearch.audit.indices LIKE ".ds-.*") AND (attributes.elasticsearch.audit.action IS NULL OR NOT attributes.elasticsearch.audit.action LIKE "*[*") | EVAL actor = COALESCE(attributes.user.email, attributes.api_key.name, attributes.user.name, "<anonymous>") | KEEP @timestamp, actor, attributes.elasticsearch.audit.indices, attributes.elasticsearch.audit.action, attributes.elasticsearch.audit.request.name, client.ip | SORT @timestamp DESC | LIMIT 1000 | RENAME @timestamp AS Time, actor AS Identity, attributes.elasticsearch.audit.indices AS Index, attributes.elasticsearch.audit.action AS `Transport action`, attributes.elasticsearch.audit.request.name AS Request, client.ip AS `Client IP`
